primary.title: Information Management: A Proposal
primary.author: Tim Berners-Lee
primary.rationale: This is the foundational document where Tim Berners-Lee first proposed the World Wide Web. It outlines the core concepts and technical specifications.

primary.title: Weaving the Web: The Original Design and Ultimate Destiny of the World Wide Web by its Inventor
primary.author: Tim Berners-Lee
primary.rationale: Berners-Lee's autobiography and reflection on the creation and evolution of the Web. It provides personal insights and historical context.

primary.title: The World Wide Web: Past, Present and Future
primary.author: Tim Berners-Lee
primary.rationale: A paper presented at the first International World Wide Web Conference, offering a retrospective and forward-looking view from the inventor.

secondary.title: Weaving the Web: The Original Design and Ultimate Destiny of the World Wide Web by its Inventor
secondary.author: Tim Berners-Lee
secondary.rationale: While authored by Berners-Lee, this book is often cited as a primary historical account and is a crucial secondary source for understanding the Web's origins from his perspective.

secondary.title: A Brief History of the World Wide Web
secondary.author: Niall Sclater
secondary.rationale: An academic article providing a concise historical overview of the World Wide Web, likely referencing Berners-Lee's contributions and foundational documents.

secondary.title: The World Wide Web: A very short introduction
secondary.author: Tim Berners-Lee
secondary.rationale: A concise overview of the Web's history, development, and impact, written by its inventor, serving as both a primary and accessible secondary source.

suggestions.notes: Tim Berners-Lee's own writings, especially his proposal and autobiography, are the most critical primary sources. Secondary sources often analyze his work and the Web's impact.
